title: Tenant upgrade fencing, config anti-entropy and live rollback guard for on-prem operator failures
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Several customers on Private/VPC saw tenant-level outages during operator/helm upgrades: helm release stuck in post-upgrade hook, controllers stalled, and tenant API 503s. Root cause analysis points to an ordering/race between Helm post-upgrade hooks and the nodeagent/KV schema handshake: the operator applied new CRs before nodeagents had finished on-disk KV schema migration, which produced a transient incompatible runtime state and reconcile failures.

Scope: Affects Private and VPC-managed on-prem tenants upgrading operator image from 1.18.x -> 1.19.x when cluster control-plane pressure or nodeagent cold-start occurs. Not a model-serving runtime bug.

Observed symptoms (customer reports & telemetry):
- Helm release upgrade enters "post-upgrade" hook and never completes (helm history shows pending-hook).
- Operator reconcile loop logs: "kv schema mismatch: expected v7 got v6" followed by repeated controller errors and reconcile backoff.
- Nodeagent CrashLoopBackOff when schema migration concurrently written by operator reconciler.
- Tenant traffic returns 503s for ~5-20 minutes until manual intervention or rollback.

Root cause: Upgrade ordering race + lack of explicit upgrade fencing. Helm applies CRs and post-upgrade hooks can trigger controller reconciles immediately; under slow nodeagent startup the operator assumes a migrated KV store. We don't have an idempotent, observable handshake that guarantees KV schema version and nodeagent readiness before completing the helm release.

Design constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Strict preflight blocks (fail upgrade if nodes not ready) reduce risk but increase upgrade friction for customers with slow clusters.
- Automatic migration during upgrade reduces manual work but must be idempotent and safe for tenants with large KV payloads.
- Rolling snapshot-and-apply approach increases S3/storage usage but provides safe rollback.

Proposed fix (short-term hotfix + medium-term improvements):
1) Hotfix operator-2025.03.1 (backwards-compatible):
   - Add upgrade fencing: operator sets a per-tenant UpgradeLock CRD annotation at helm pre-upgrade hook and refuses to mark upgrade complete until nodeagent readiness + KV version handshake succeed.
   - Implement an idempotent "schema-check-and-noop-migrate" controller that detects schema mismatches and either triggers an orchestrated migration job or places tenant into a read-only fence state until migration completes.
   - Before any potentially-destructive manifest apply, take a lightweight snapshot of tenant KV metadata (not full blobs) and store to S3/GCS with tenant-id + timestamp for rollback reference.
   - Improve helm-hook detection: add a post-upgrade probe that verifies operator-level handshakes have completed before returning success to helm.
2) Medium-term (after hotfix):
   - Upstream a staged KV migration library used by nodeagent to allow in-place, chunked migrations with progress markers.
   - Add CI upgrade tests that simulate slow nodeagent start and validate fencing semantics.

Rollback safety and runbook (hotfix behavior and manual rollback steps):
- If a helm upgrade is stuck: use `kubectl annotate tenant <T> redwood.io/upgrade-action=rollback-request` to trigger guarded rollback flow. This will: abort in-flight migration jobs, restore lightweight KV snapshot, and trigger `helm rollback` followed by reconcile requeue.
- Runbook steps (short version):
  1) Identify affected tenants via console -> "Upgrade failures" dashboard. Note release and cluster.
  2) Check operator logs for "upgrade-lock" and "kv schema mismatch" messages.
  3) If upgrade in post-upgrade hook, follow rollback-request command above.
  4) If stuck due to migration job, run `kubectl -n redwood get jobs | grep migration-<tenant>` and inspect job logs, then either allow to finish or trigger job cancel + restore snapshot.
  5) For customer comms: inform customer of rollback and expected RTO (15-45 minutes).

Testing plan:
- Integration: create CI job that runs helm upgrade under controlled nodeagent-start delays (simulate 5s/30s/120s delays). Validate helm completes only when handshake succeeds.
- Load testing: ensure migration job chunking prevents node OOM for large tenants.
- Chaos testing: kill nodeagent mid-upgrade to validate idempotent resume.

Release plan and metrics to monitor during rollout:
- Release tag: operator-2025.03.1-hotfix. Canary rollout: 5% of dedicated clusters (low-impact tenants) -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours if no regressions.
- Metrics: operator.reconcile_errors (count), helm.upgrade_failures, tenant.api_503_rate, nodeagent.restart_count, kv.migration_duration_p95. Alert thresholds defined in Console runbook.

Customer communication: Drafted email template for SEs & CSMs linking to incident timeline, mitigation steps, and expected upgrade window.

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Upgrade+Fencing+and+KV+Handshake, GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/7891, CI test: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/operator-upgrade-fencing/42, Slack thread: #onprem-upgrades (msg id 162044).
